text:
[LCST.4.3.4] **A `null` source converts to `null`, and the conversion is
not attempted.** Where the source value of a `::T?` is `null`, the result is
`null`: the runtime must not hand the absent value to the conversion, and must
not raise. This holds for every defined conversion ([LCST.4.5.2]), whatever its
fallibility, and it is what makes [LCST.4.3.1]'s nullable rows mean anything —
the `?` on `S? … ::T?` exists to carry exactly this case, and a runtime that
refused it would make a legal program unrunnable the first time the slot was
absent.

The result feeds `??`, Kleene logic and narrowing as any other `T?` does
([LCST.4.3.3]), so a cast propagates absence the way an operator does
([LNUL.4.1]) rather than ending the activation.

**This is not [LCST.4.5.4]'s trap.** That carve-out is for a source **value**
the target cannot represent — a `Float` with no `Int`, to `Int` — which is a value
the conversion was handed and could not convert. `null` is the absence of a
value, so there is nothing to represent and nothing to trap.

idris.name: lcst_4_2__cast
idris.note: A null operand under ::T? is null and reaches no conversion: `lcst_4_5_2__convert` is not applied to it, whatever the target.

idris.name: lcst_4_3_4__null_source_converts_to_null
idris.note: For every target, a null source converts to null and nothing is raised.
